title: Prove a fixed-tape lowering for the selected BIT caller
body:
I give a source-level fixed-tape lowering of the all-size p=1 BIT caller in David Arias's PR2753. The construction replaces depth-dependent frame tapes and generator returns with permanent roles, shared numerical banks, sequential parking and a finite return label. Under the pinned caller's input and root-coupling hypotheses, I prove O_q(V_root)+F_q physical space and retain its O_q(V(n+w)) local toll.

I implement the actual numerical Frame substitution, stream-role parking and serialized residual cursors. The whole-caller result uses the explicit macroprogram/refinement proof in PROOF.md; I have not generated its complete transition table. The complete small payload test retains the logical payload scheduler.

Validation covers:

- The actual selected Frame boundary, normal return and two injected failure paths, with exact parent Word identity/value/head restoration.
- 16,362 reference trace events, 180 serialized cursor reconstructions and 1,500 nested stream/numerical checkpoints with a protected output port.
- A complete 9,216-address GL2 recursive payload, 12 shared-bank child calls and 156 residuals.

The stronger H2 primitives, outer borrowing wrapper and supplier transfer remain separate obligations. I make no exponent improvement or selected-frontier change. The package retains 97 byte-exact source exports and their notices. I credit David Arias for PR2753, ywz65 for PR2635 and my PR2769 numerical codec. I used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; I claim no independent human or proof-assistant review.

All five registered commands passed under Python 3.12.15, including normal and optimized Frame/continuation runs. The complete GL2 payload took 150.31 seconds. After fast-forwarding to canonical main `28f54620ff770dd051d5df35882bd84303d13c6f`, I authenticated all inputs again; the runner and proof-relevant inputs had no changes.

Coordination: [scoped claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18958887).

Reproduce with Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-physical-caller
```
